Simplified form of 頁.  Pictograph of a head (首) on top of a person (卩). Means "head" when pronounced xié. Has unrelated meaning "leaf" when pronounced yè, due to this character being adopted as a shorthand form of 葉.
From cursive script of 頁 /页.

A person's head
Pictograph of a head (首) on top of a person (卩). Means "head" when pronounced xié. Has unrelated meaning "leaf" when pronounced yè, due to this character being adopted as a shorthand form of 葉.
頭也。从𦣻从几。古文䭫首如此。凡頁之屬皆从頁。𦣻者，䭫首字也。

Pictogram (象形): 首 + 卩 – head of a kneeling person, emphasising “head”.
頁 and 首 (OC *hljuʔ, *hljus) were originally the same pictographic character with the same meaning of “head”, and the graphical difference was that 頁 also included the body in addition to the head of the person.
頁 was later used as an alternative popular form of 葉 (“leaf; page”) to mean “sheet; page (of paper)”, which is its main meaning today.
The original sense of “head” is preserved in the radical 頁, which is used in characters such as 頭 (“head”) and 頸 (“neck”).
Alternative form of 葉 /叶 (“leaf; sheet (of paper)”).
Original meaning of this character.
頭也。从𦣻从几。古文䭫首如此。凡頁之屬皆从頁。𦣻者，䭫首字也。

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database describes 頁 in oracle and bronze forms as 卩 plus 首: a kneeling human figure with the head visually prominent. It says the graph denotes ‘head’; 頁 and 首 differ in whether the body is drawn and are graphic variants. Its examples include oracle-bone uses meaning ‘pig’s head’ (合集15684) and ‘bowing the head’ (合集22215); it notes a Western Zhou bronze occurrence in 卯簋蓋 and a phrase 頁手 there, possibly abbreviated or erroneous. It reports that 頁 and 首 were originally one graph pronounced like 首, and that 頁 had acquired the reading 胡結切 by the Eastern Han at the latest. The source calls the paper measure use a俗字 for 葉. Its account of shape change says oracle-bone 頁 may show or omit hair; a W. Zhou bronze has hair; Warring States forms often distort the hair as 止; the small-seal form omits it. This is a database’s paleographic analysis, not direct visual inspection in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.field: 說文解字；音韻方言；字源字形
evidence.text: The page reproduces the Shuowen entry 頁, ‘head’, analyzed as from 𦣻 and 儿, and gives 胡結切. It also reproduces Duan Yucai’s note disputing the received wording and explaining the entry as an old form associated with 䭬/首; this records a later textual-critical interpretation, not a settled ancient graphic analysis. The page lists oracle-bone examples (including 乙8780 and 合22217), a mid-Western Zhou bronze 卯簋蓋, Chu bamboo-and-silk examples, a Shuowen small-seal form, and Eastern Han clerical evidence. Its dictionary explains the paper/page use as俗用頁 for 葉 and quotes Qing scholar Zhu Junsheng’s statement that 葉 was the proper graph and 頁 was the common form.
evidence.title: 頁 yè、xié - 漢典

evidence.field: Chinese > Glyph origin; pronunciation; Old Chinese
evidence.text: This opened secondary lexicon reports a pictographic analysis combining 卩 and 首, says 頁 and 首 were originally the same head pictograph with the body included in the 頁 form, and reports 頁 used by Eastern Han as a popular alternative for 葉 with paper-sheet/page meaning. It lists modern Mandarin yè for the page sense and xié for head, and Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese /*leb/ and /*ɡleːd/ under two readings. Treat these as the page’s compiled claims; the CUHK character-specific analysis independently supports the broad distinction between the head graph and paper-use spelling, but not every reconstruction or precise dating claim.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone and bronze 頁 as combining 卩 and 首, depicting a kneeling human with the head emphasized. It describes 頁 and 首 as graphic variants distinguished by whether the body is drawn, and reports oracle-bone examples for the head sense: 合集15684 豕頁 (“pig’s head”) and 合集22215 五子叩頁 (“the boys bow their heads”). Its shape account says oracle-bone forms may include or omit hair, a Western Zhou bronze form has hair, Warring States forms often distort the hair into 止, and the small-seal form omits it. It treats the paper measure use as a common form for 葉 and reports a change to 胡結切 by the Eastern Han at the latest. This is the database’s analysis, not a direct inspection of the ancient artifacts.

evidence.text: The entry identifies 頁 as U+9801 and gives the Shuowen gloss 頭也 and 胡結切; it also lists Guangyun 胡結. Its analysis describes 頁 as head-plus-body pictography and cites oracle-bone contexts for the head sense. It cautions that the bronze phrase 頁手 appears only once and may be abbreviated or erroneous. It says 頁 and 首 were originally one graph and that the graph’s paper measure sense is a common form for 葉. The head-sense evidence and paper-use account are separate; the page does not establish the earliest dated instance of the latter.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The official Unicode Unihan lookup pages for U+9801 and U+9875 were attempted but inaccessible; supplied local kMandarin rows are not substituted for verified external click-through evidence.

The proposed adoption of 頁 as a common spelling for 葉 in the page/sheet sense is supported as a lexicographic account, but this research did not independently identify and verify the earliest dated attestation of that borrowed use or a full sequence of dated semantic extensions.

The head reading xié is supported lexicographically and by the cited Guangyun fanqie, while the page-use yè is also recorded; this work did not independently establish the historical sound path behind their separate readings. Do not conflate the page-word borrowing with the graphic origin of the head pictograph.
No claims are made here about a sound component: 頁 is analyzed as a pictographic graph in its head sense, while page/sheet use is a whole-graph borrowing or common-form substitution for 葉.

CUHK reports a possible error/abbreviation in the isolated bronze phrase 頁手; the intended reading is uncertain. Shuowen’s component wording is also text-critically disputed in the reproduced Duan Yucai note.
Glyph images were not visually inspected during this research; graphic descriptions are attributed to the opened database and dictionary analyses.

The earliest dated attestation of 頁 used for 葉’s page/sheet sense and a dated sequence of subsequent extensions were not established. The database calls this a common form for 葉, not a graphic development from the head pictograph.
The dataset’s reported Eastern Han latest bound for the 胡結切 reading concerns the head graph’s reading history and does not date the page/sheet usage.
The identity of the referents behind individual oracle-bone examples is reported through the database’s interpretation; no artifact image was independently inspected in this research.
The bronze phrase 頁手 is uncertain: the source considers abbreviation or error possible.
Duan Yucai’s challenge to the received Shuowen component wording is a textual-critical interpretation; the exact ancient formation cannot be settled from the received Shuowen gloss alone.
The official Unicode lookup pages for both U+9801 and U+9875 were inaccessible. The supplied local reading rows are recorded as local provenance only.
The Xiaoxuetang query did not yield a usable character-specific form image, and its precise official CC0 notice could not be opened in this pass; no image from that database is selected.
The second local Commons lead, File:Shuowen Seal Radical 324.svg, could not be accessed as an exact Commons description page, so it is not proposed.
